Pitch decks that make sense

A strong pitch explains the business and its evidence. Beautiful slides cannot rescue unclear economics.

Pitch decks that make senseBIZZINTEL · KEEP BUILDING
How to use this guide

Read one lesson, complete the action in your business, and keep the result somewhere you can find it. The examples are illustrations, not claims about real customers.

LESSON 01 / 05

Decide who the pitch is for

Banks, grant panels, partners and investors have different questions.

What to do

  1. Identify judges, partner, bank or investor audience.
  2. State the decision you want them to make.
  3. Prepare a 90-second version before making slides.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: a grant panel needs impact, need and delivery feasibility; an investor focuses on economics and scalable returns.

AVOID THIS

Copying generic advice without checking that it fits your market, customer and costs.

↗
What you should finish with

Pitch brief.

Evidence to capture: Your written output or link to the relevant source
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Create a pitch brief for my chosen audience. Clarify what I am asking for, why now, and what evidence the audience will need.
LESSON 02 / 05

Build the story

The deck needs an argument, not random slides.

What to do

  1. Follow Problem → Impact/Story → Opportunity → Numbers → Ask.
  2. Select a maximum of one central claim per slide.
  3. Write presenter talk tracks, not walls of text.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Example to adapt: describe what a real customer would do or see at this step. Use actual facts for your business.

AVOID THIS

Copying generic advice without checking that it fits your market, customer and costs.

↗
What you should finish with

10–12 slide storyline.

Evidence to capture: Your written output or link to the relevant source
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Outline a persuasive 10-slide business pitch for my market and audience. Mark any missing market-size, traction or financial figures as evidence needed.
LESSON 03 / 05

Document the numbers

Funders will question unsupported projections.

What to do

  1. Check total need, usage of funds and what the money unlocks.
  2. Show real pricing, cost and key assumptions.
  3. Practice explaining how numbers were derived.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Example to adapt: describe what a real customer would do or see at this step. Use actual facts for your business.

AVOID THIS

Copying generic advice without checking that it fits your market, customer and costs.

↗
What you should finish with

Assumption-backed financial slides.

Evidence to capture: Your written output or link to the relevant source
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Design clear, defensible financial and use-of-funds slides with blank inputs for unsupported numbers.
LESSON 04 / 05

Create your visuals

Slides should make the story easier to absorb.

What to do

  1. Use actual product photos, examples, simple charts, limited copy and consistent branding.
  2. Record the result in your workbook.
  3. Verify important details before treating the task as finished.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Example to adapt: describe what a real customer would do or see at this step. Use actual facts for your business.

AVOID THIS

Copying generic advice without checking that it fits your market, customer and costs.

↗
What you should finish with

Visual brief for every slide.

Evidence to capture: Your written output or link to the relevant source
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Provide a clean visual direction and presenter notes for every slide, with no invented business evidence.
LESSON 05 / 05

Prepare for questions

The discussion is part of the pitch.

What to do

  1. Answer what happens if growth is slower than expected.
  2. Explain why this team can deliver.
  3. Be able to explain the business and ask in 90 seconds.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Example to adapt: describe what a real customer would do or see at this step. Use actual facts for your business.

AVOID THIS

Copying generic advice without checking that it fits your market, customer and costs.

↗
What you should finish with

Investor or partner Q&A sheet.

Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋
